chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a slave who cut off the hand of a free man, while three fingers of that hand were paralyzed. He said: “And what is the value of the slave?” I said: “Set it at whatever you wish.”

He said: “If the value of the slave is greater than the indemnity of the two sound fingers and the three paralyzed fingers, then the one whose hand was cut shall return to the guardian of the slave whatever exceeds the value, and take the slave. And if he wishes, he may take the value of the two sound fingers and the three paralyzed fingers.”

I said: “How much is the value of the two sound fingers and the three fingers?” He said: “The value of the two sound fingers together with the palm is two thousand dirhams, and the value of the three paralyzed fingers together with the palm is one thousand dirhams, because they are assessed at one-third of the indemnity of sound ones.”

He said: “And if the value of the slave is less than the value of the two sound fingers and the three paralyzed fingers, the slave is handed over to the one whose hand was cut, or his master may ransom him and take back the slave.”

key_terms.دِيَةِ: financial indemnity owed for bodily injury
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave, whose financial value affects legal liability in this ruling
key_terms.قِيمَةُ: the market value or assessed worth used in legal calculation
key_terms.وَلِيِّ: the guardian or legal authority responsible for the slave
key_terms.يَفْتَدِيَهُ: to ransom him, meaning the master pays to recover the slave
key_terms.ٱلشَّلَلِ: paralysis, which reduces the compensation value of the affected fingers
key_terms.ٱلْإِصْبَعَيْنِ: the two sound fingers whose compensation is calculated at the normal rate
key_terms.ٱلْكَفِّ: the palm, included in the valuation alongside the fingers

ai.seo_question: How is compensation calculated in Shia fiqh when a slave injures the partially paralyzed hand of a free person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on compensation when a slave cuts the hand of a free man whose hand already had three paralyzed fingers. It explains how to calculate the indemnity for the sound and paralyzed fingers and how the slave’s market value affects whether the injured party takes the slave or receives compensation. The report is significant for detailed judicial rulings concerning injury, valuation, and liability.
